sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art: Islamic Art of the Deccan
sources.note: Direct essay read. Nizam Shahi dynasty 1490 to 1636, regional courts and arts. Its compressed statement about Mughal rule after 1600 is not adopted; regional resistance is separately sourced.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India: Tomb of Ahmad Shah
sources.note: Direct official monument entry read; founder, reign and architecture.

sources.title: George Michell and Mark Zebrowski: Miniature painting, Ahmadnagar and Bijapur
sources.note: Original scholarly chapter publisher preview read, The Architecture and Art of the Deccan Sultanates, chapter 5, pp.145 to 190. Opening discussion of Tarif-i Husain Shahi, January 1565 campaign and queen.

sources.title: Courtney Stewart, The Met: Feminine Power in the Deccan
sources.note: Direct essay read. Only Chand Bibi material used; the separate eighteenth-century Mah Laqa Bai discussion is not projected into Ahmadnagar.

sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art: Habshi and Sidi
sources.note: Direct specialist museum essay read: Malik Ambar, enslavement, freedom, military and dynastic ties. Apparent Ahmadabad/Ahmadnagar typo in owner description is not adopted.

sources.title: Maharashtra State Gazetteers: Ahmadnagar, places of interest
sources.note: Original state page read through indexed full-section excerpts after direct fetch timeouts. Locators Channels; Nepti and Nimbgaon channels; Behisht Bagh. Later municipal repairs, 1884 consumption and nineteenth-century latrines are not treated as Nizam Shahi evidence. Reproducible query: site:gazetteers.maharashtra.gov.in "Nepti" "hamamkhana".

sources.title: M. R. Singh and S. Vinodh Kumar: Architectural features and characterization of Farah Bagh
sources.note: Original research full text read at ResearchGate article 332935786; DOI publisher access limited. Sections 3.2, discussion and conclusions, pp.7 and 12 to 13. Material observations only: article introduction mislabels the palace as late-fifteenth-century Mughal; those historical labels are not adopted. Moisture/cooling function is the authors’ interpretation.

sources.title: A. A. Kadiri: Some More Direction-Stones of the Nizam Shahi Dynasty
sources.note: Original ASI Epigraphia Indica, Arabic and Persian Supplement 1970 (published 1975), pp.45 to 62. Downloaded and visually inspected pp.49 to 50, PDF pages81 to 82. Inscription 2 at Bir, Persian text and translation p.50; printed spelling احمدانگر differs from normalized search text احمدنگر. Inscription 1 royal instruction to erect signs at road junctions, p.49.

sources.title: The Met: Sultans of Deccan India, 1500 to 1700, catalogue 17, Royal Picnic
sources.note: Downloaded original 2015 exhibition catalogue; Navina Najat Haidar, cat.17, printed p.68/PDF page85. British Library Add.Or.3004, ca.1590 to 95. Named sitter and diplomats are uncertain. Existing Bahmani card also cites this PDF; cumulative use checked.

sources.title: Fabrizio Speziale: Indo-Muslim Physicians, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct specialist article read, paragraph beginning The activities of Indo-Persian medical writers, Nizam Shahi court and Firishta. Dynasty endpoint in this compressed paragraph is not used.

sources.title: Maharashtra State Gazetteers: Ahmadnagar, Mediaeval Period
sources.note: Original indexed excerpts read: 1600 fort capture, continuation under Malik Ambar and Mian Raju; final Shahaji campaign and submission within three months after 11 July 1636. Direct page access timed out.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India: Ancient India 5, epigraphical discoveries
sources.note: Original ASI indexed text, printed p.60, Satmala hill-fort inscriptions dated AH1045/1046 (1636), naming fourteen captured forts and Allah Vardi Khan Turkman. Day-level discrepancy with a chronicle is not used.

sources.title: Maharashtra State Gazetteers: Ahmadnagar under the Moghals
sources.note: Original indexed state text read: post-1636 union of Ahmadnagar and Khandesh governments, Aurangzeb as viceroy, Murshid Quli Khan and Shivaji’s claims. Explicitly later history.

proposedOverrides.name: Ahmadnagar (Nizam Shahi Sultanate)
proposedOverrides.summary: A Deccan sultanate remembered through water channels, court scholarship, paintings and bilingual road signs. Its Nizam Shahi dynasty ended in 1636, before the imported map cutoff.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One exact indexed Nizam Shahi polity, no aliases. Historical dynasty 1490 to 1636; imported 1492 to 1700 retained as map coverage. Post-1636 period and passage are explicitly later Mughal/Maratha context.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Five decoded polygons span 1492 to 1700. First four retain almost identical very broad bounds, roughly 72.79E to 78.57E and 16.62N to 23.90N; final northern extent falls to 21.11N. These are not reliable changing Nizam Shahi frontiers; public opening warns that the outline persists beyond sovereignty.
batchIdentityNotes.evidence: identity.json records exact decoded features and missing-card/override/staged collision check. Dynastic dates are supported by Met and state gazetteer; final settlement uses the Ahmadnagar gazetteer’s 1636 chronology rather than inconsistent older 1637 shorthand.
batchIdentityNotes.scope: Court and urban water evidence is much richer than ordinary household evidence. Bath is explicitly elite; physician access and picnic custom are not generalized. Nineteenth-century municipal latrines and water-use figures deliberately excluded.
